data.name: Jellyfish
data.detailed_description:
Jellyfish is a game which tells you a story.
The story takes place in the depth of the ocean where the player takes the shape of a simple jellyfish.
Jellyfish presents the full life cycle of a jellyfish, a soft bodied, free-swimming aquatic animal with a gelatinous umbrella-shaped bell and trailing tentacles.
Most people are only familiar with the full-grown jellyfish, the translucent, bell-shaped creatures that occasionally wash up on beaches and swim almost in every ocean on earth.
And yet jellyfish have several very complex life cycles, in which they go through a number of different developmental stages that are presented in Jellyfish(this game).
As the story goes, the player will guide and accompany the jellyfish from it's very birth to the very end of it's journey.
Using the arrows(or WASD keys) to eat, solve various puzzles, fight hostile creatures, and then to chase a suitable mate, *and then find new life soaring the skies on a flying snail*.

Features:

1.The game features 10 different levels.
The first two levels are mostly a casual game, the next two are more of a puzzle game, and then comes an RPG game.

2.Control the jellyfish using the arrow keys(or the WASD keys) to guide it through it's journey.

3. Jellyfish is designed as an "art game".
All the characters within the game are created by complex programming math codes, the movement is designed to be as smooth and elegant as possible.

4. This is a short game, a work of interactive art, which bring the most beautiful animal to your screen.

**Just like a painting of a sunflower on the rough canvas, imagine a jellyfish on your computer screen.
Jellyfish are among the most handsome and unique beings in our world, just like the growing flowers.
I have made this game to demonstrate how rich, deep, unique and beautiful our life is.**

data.short_description: A simulation game about the life story of a jellyfish. In this game, I will present the full life cycle of a jellyfish: from an egg to a hydra and finally, after a not very long journey it becomes an adult jellyfish. A work of interactive art to bring the most beautiful of sea creatures to your screen.

reviews.review:
I have been assured that while achievements are NOT currently available, they will be available soon.-  (9/16/17)

During the late 1960s – early 1970s a trend started to develop of various forms of art being integrated with contemporary music. We started to see bands like The Velvet Underground, under sponsorship of the enigmatic artist, Andy Warhol, combining art, video and sound to great international success. A decade later we saw The Talking heads do something similar, made up entirely of art students presenting music within their artistic expression. In between, we had “art rockers” creating music artistically in the persons of Klaus Nomi, Roxy Music, and many more, blurring the lines between performance art and rock and roll.

And now we increasingly see computers used to create and present art, and computer gaming further blurring the distinction of where games end and art begins….if it actually ends at all. A game such as PANORAMICAL is likely more truly art than game, and is capable of creaing great beauty and music together, in a manner unique to each “player”. And of course, games such as ANTICHAMBER or KAIRO have been both immensely popular and well received. But which itch do they best scratch; game or art? But perhaps better yet, they bring a strong aspect of art into the lives of gamers that might otherwise be mostly devoid of such expression.

And we have a new developer on Steam who also has a strong commitment to art, comparing his need for art to that of food. Going by the name of “romeosoft”, Chinese artist and developer PanGuoJun is already a successful artist, primarily with the computer as his “brush” :   https://fineartamerica.com/profiles/guojun-pan.html .

He currently has three games on Steam; PLANTON, which is described as a plankton simulation, or “electronic pet”, FLOWER DESIGN, a beautiful and fascinating tool for learning and utilizing the centuries-old Asian art of minimalistic flower arrangement, and now, JELLYFISH.

JELLYFISH is described as essentially an art installation relating the life cycle of a specific jellyfish from conception to the beginning of the next, continuing cycle of life. But while the story is told in the form of a game, each of 10 stages is told in a different manner, whichever the artist felt was most appropriate to illustrate each cycle artistically. And that is where the artistic expression comes in. While the arcade-style play in each level is not necessarily new, what is new Is presenting it as art, specific to how each level is best told in the opinion of the artist/developer.

An additional aspect of this game that is critical to its impact is the remarkable soundtrack by Axidious. While providing much to any game, the best soundtracks provide impact in a subtle manner, reaching through to the player at the most critical moments. Though brief (to fit the game) this soundtrack succeeds with the best..

JELLYFISH is short, about 30- 45 minutes, and seemingly brief with deliberation. The point isn’t to create something of size, but rather of beauty. Some of the levels pass quickly, almost before the player knows they’ve begun, and are very easy (much like life), while other levels are complicated and longer in duration. (Again, representing life.) Those players who appreciate indie developers, and something a bit out of the norm (as has been very popular on many previous occasions) may find something here of unusual value and meaning without spending a lot of money for it. (And they may even learn something about the beauty of life, and life cycles, along the way.)
